addition.item: Background videos per slide from YouTube, Vimeo or a video file (MP4, WebM): muted, without controls, loaded only when the slide is shown and faded in once playing; the image is the poster. Videos pause with the Pause button, off-screen and in hidden tabs. YouTube uses youtube-nocookie.com and Vimeo Do Not Track.
Facebook videos: Facebook doesn't allow muted background videos, so a Facebook link adds a Play video button that opens the video in a lightbox; the slideshow pauses meanwhile.

"Wait until a slide's video has ended": autoplay moves on when the video ends (YouTube, Vimeo and video files) and the progress bar and navigation follow the video. Videos that don't start within 10 seconds use the slide's duration.
YOOtheme's cookie consent: YouTube and Vimeo videos wait for consent and start as soon as it is given; until then the image shows.
"Play videos on phones" can be switched off to show the image and save data. With reduced motion the image shows instead of the video.

Presets: Corporate Hero, Product Showcase, Split Story, Testimonial and Minimal Fade. A preset sets the layout, transition, image effects, text styles, animation and navigation and hides those settings; heights, colours, durations and content stay yours.

Transitions Wipe, Curtain, Circle reveal, Diagonal and Blinds: the new slide is drawn over the old one, which recedes slightly. Swiping still changes the slide; with reduced motion they become a fade.

Split layout: the image beside a panel in the theme's default, muted, primary or secondary colour (the text colour follows the panel). Half, 60% or two thirds wide; each slide can put its image on the other side. The image comes in from the panel's edge; on phones it is on top and the slideshow is at least 640px tall.
Content card behind the text: Box, Glass, Primary or Secondary.
Button icons (before or after the text) and an Arrow Icon for your own arrows; both can be Icon Pro icons.
A Shape Divider of Shape Dividers Pro shown in front at the bottom of the section: the content, navigation and progress bar move up to make room for it.
Navigation styles: Dots, Lines with progress, Slide titles with progress (each slide can have a short Navigation Title) and Thumbnails with progress. On phones titles and thumbnails become lines.
Navigation position: bottom centre, start or end over the slides, or below the slideshow in the section's colours.
Counter (01 / 05).

Progress bar on the top or bottom edge that fills while a slide is shown and stops with the autoplay; without autoplay it shows how far through the slides the visitor is. Colour: Auto (the slide's text colour), primary, secondary or a gradient from the primary colour (to the secondary colour, or to a lighter primary when the secondary colour is grey); thickness 1-8px.
Arrow styles Minimal, Circle, Square and Glass; arrows on the sides or together beside the navigation; side arrows on hover only.

change.item: The Dots checkbox became the Navigation setting; slideshows with dots turned off keep no navigation.

addition.item: First release: a hero slideshow built on UIkit, each slide with an eyebrow, title, content, two buttons, an image and an image for phones. Slides can come from dynamic content such as articles.
The eyebrow, title, text and buttons come in one after another on every slide: fade up, slide in, blur in, mask reveal or word by word, with delay, stagger and duration.
Ken Burns zoom in, zoom out, pan left, pan right or alternating, per slide too.
Overlay in black, white, the theme's primary or secondary colour or a custom colour, solid, as a gradient from the bottom or the side, or as a vignette.
Height: full screen (minus the header), a ratio or fixed; content in nine positions inside the page container, light or dark text per slide (the header follows).
Autoplay with its own duration per slide; it pauses on hover and focus, when the slideshow is off-screen or the tab is hidden, and with a Pause/Play button.
Show from/until dates per slide; the builder preview shows scheduled slides marked.
Focal point for the image and the phone image; the first image loads first.
The first slide's title can be the page's H1, the others H2.
Arrows, dots and a scroll-down hint for full-screen slideshows.
